::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING V1 candidate

This page defines the dev35 candidate for static capacitance evaluation and
its JAX sensitivities. It does not change the existing dynamic S/Y/Z or
residue-normalized-coupling contracts. The implementation and this public
contract remain `CONVERGING` until the Human accepts this scope.
:::

## Scope

This candidate covers single-effective-point matrix and element `evaluate()`
requests, plus the required existing Jacobian, JVP, and VJP Sensitivity
requests for those outputs. It makes no additional claim for
`ParameterSpace` sweeps, optimization, warmup, or detached `prepare()`
functions. Quantization, nonlinear elements, second-order derivatives, and
EC/frequency calculations remain outside this scope.

## Public declarations

```text
StaticCapacitanceSpec(zero_charge=())
StaticCapacitanceSpec.matrix
StaticCapacitanceSpec.element(*, row, column)
StaticCapacitanceElementSpec.value
```

`StaticCapacitanceSpec` asks for the complete compiled static capacitance
matrix on one Plan, one effective parameter point, and one supported View.
Its default `zero_charge=()` requests the full matrix. The same declaration can
name an explicit zero-charge coordinate partition:

```python
matrix_spec = StaticCapacitanceSpec()
entry_spec = matrix_spec.element(row=row_coordinate, column=column_coordinate)
reduced_spec = StaticCapacitanceSpec(zero_charge=(eliminated_coordinate,))
```

`matrix_spec.matrix` selects the matrix as a sensitivity leaf. An element spec's
`.value` selects its scalar entry. Both selectors support the ordinary
`.on(view)` binding used by `SensitivitySpec`. For direct evaluation, pass the
matrix or element spec to `run.evaluate(view, spec)`:

```python
matrix_result = run.evaluate(view, matrix_spec, parameters=point)
entry_result = run.evaluate(view, entry_spec, parameters=point)
```

The matrix result exposes `matrix` as a Pint Quantity in farads, ordered
`row_coordinates` and `column_coordinates`, its `zero_charge` partition, and
evidence bound to the Plan, effective point, View, dtype, and realized finite
discretization. The element result exposes its scalar `value` in farads, row and
column identities, the same partition, and the same provenance. Coordinate
axes use the complete compiled node-coordinate basis of the selected View; they
are not restricted to RF Ports.

These returned row and column IDs, including internal finite-pi axes, can
address a later static element or `zero_charge` request for the same Plan,
View, effective parameter point, and realized mesh. This is static-output-axis
addressing only: it does not create public `CoordinateRef` values or grant
internal coordinates access through RF selectors or `retain()`.

Each request evaluates one effective `ParameterSet` on the same sealed Plan.
Omitted physical parameters use the Plan's captured baselines. The result is a
detached in-memory value or is written and read through the ordinary Workspace
path. A returned Result keeps its fixed read ownership and remains readable
after `run.close()`.

## Coordinate and charge convention

The physical finite capacitance matrix is $C_x$ in the current View's ordered
coordinate basis. An existing supported real, dimensionless coordinate
transform maps coordinates as $x=T(\theta)y$, where the current parameter point
determines any existing transform weights. The transformed matrix is the
congruence

$$
C_y(\theta)=T(\theta)^T C_x(\theta)T(\theta).
$$

This is a static charge relation, $q=Cv$; it is not a frequency response or a
sampled low-frequency approximation to S, Y, or Z. The compiled finite model is
the one actually used by the request, including the capacitors of a finite-pi
transmission-line realization.

For an explicit `zero_charge` set, let $e$ be those coordinates and let $r$ be
the remaining coordinates in the selected View's original order. Partition the
transformed matrix as

$$
C_y=\begin{bmatrix}C_{rr}&C_{re}\\C_{er}&C_{ee}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The returned retained-coordinate matrix follows the zero-charge condition
$q_e=0$:

$$
C_{\mathrm{eff}}=C_{rr}-C_{re}\,\operatorname{solve}(C_{ee},C_{er}).
$$

The eliminated coordinates are not newly grounded or assigned a hidden clamp;
the condition is zero charge. The empty partition returns the complete matrix
without an elimination solve. The result records the selected partition and
ordered retained axes.

## Sensitivity and discrete realization

The existing `SensitivitySpec` supports `Jacobian`, `JVP`, and `VJP` for both
the matrix and an element. Bind each selected leaf to the intended View:

```python
quantities = {"C": matrix_spec.matrix.on(view)}
sensitivity_spec = SensitivitySpec(
    quantities=quantities,
    wrt=(capacitance_parameter,),
    derivative=Jacobian(),
    discretization=fixed_mesh,
)
sensitivity = run.sensitivity(sensitivity_spec, parameters=point)
```

The derivative follows the actual parameter-dependent physical matrix, the
existing transform weights $T(\theta)$, and the specified square solve. The
operation does not freeze transform weights at a baseline or stop gradients at
the elimination boundary. Jacobian output axes identify the matrix row and
column coordinates; scalar elements retain their row and column identities.
The existing sensitivity layout carries parameter and output units: a raw
matrix Jacobian cell has units of farads per SI unit of the requested input.
An F/F derivative is dimensionless because of those units; it is not
automatically normalized or scaled. JVP and VJP use the same selected physical
output and ordinary direction/cotangent unit rules described in the
[Sensitivity guide](../guides/sensitivity.qmd).

Integer mesh choices remain discrete. A sensitivity request binds one fixed
realized mesh; derivatives do not differentiate a section-count decision or
remesh along a perturbation. The saved result records the mesh used for its
finite capacitance model.

## Failure and backend boundary

The complete matrix can be returned even when it is singular. If the requested
zero-charge elimination requires a singular or otherwise unsolved $C_{ee}$,
the native linear solve failure is reported. The operation does not use a
pseudoinverse, diagonal clamp, guessed reference node, or regularization to
manufacture a reduced value.

The supported View is the original View or an existing coordinate-transform-
only View. PTC and retained/dynamically Schur-reduced Views are outside this
static-capacitance scope; a request on one fails explicitly rather than
changing the requested matrix meaning. The initial backend support is JAX.
Explicit Julia static-capacitance requests fail as unsupported; this does not
change the capabilities of existing Julia operations.

The same physical couplings and existing residue-normalized-coupling
definition, including its RF branch inputs and meaning, continue to govern
their current operations.

For usage, see the [static capacitance guide](../guides/static-capacitance.qmd).
